name: Ash Veil Cultist
description:
An Ash Veil Cultist is a gaunt, unsettling figure wrapped in layered charcoal robes dusted with gray soot, as though it has walked through a funeral pyre and never bothered to clean the ashes away. Its face is usually hidden behind a veil of smoke-stained linen or a lacquered half-mask marked with thin white sigils, leaving only the glint of fever-bright eyes visible in the gloom. Charred cords, sealed tokens, and strips of prayer paper hang from its belt like trophies taken from a sacrificial rite. When it moves, it does so with quiet purpose, fingers stained black with ash and ink, as if it has spent years handling censers, burned records, and forbidden relics.

In the Curated Quarter, such cultists blend unnervingly well among scribes and traders, their reverent manners masking fanatic devotion. They speak softly, often in coded phrases about purification, concealment, and the "necessary burning" of false histories. Around them lingers the scent of smoke, wax, and old paper, and lanternlight seems to dim in their presence. In ritual gatherings, they scatter ash in careful circles, invoking hidden wards, erased names, and the ruin beneath Numillian's polished surface. Their stillness is the most alarming thing about them: patient, watchful, and certain that all secrets must eventually be reduced to ash.
